title: Surface Integrals, Divergence Theorem & Stokes Theorem

sections.heading: Surface Integrals, Divergence Theorem & Stokes Theorem Practice Exercises

questions.q: Find \( \nabla\cdot\mathbf F \) at \( \left( 2, \  1, \  0\right) \) for \( \mathbf F=\langle y e^{x}, x z, y z^{2} \rangle \).
questions.answer: \( \nabla\cdot\mathbf F=2 y z + y e^{x} \); at \( \left( 2, \  1, \  0\right) \) this is \( e^{2} \).

questions.q: Find \( \nabla\cdot\mathbf F \) at \( \left( 2, \  -2, \  1\right) \) for \( \mathbf F=\langle x z, y z, x y \rangle \).
questions.answer: \( \nabla\cdot\mathbf F=2 z \); at \( \left( 2, \  -2, \  1\right) \) this is \( 2 \).

questions.q: Find \( \nabla\cdot\mathbf F \) at \( \left( 2, \  -2, \  0\right) \) for \( \mathbf F=\langle y e^{x}, x z, y z^{2} \rangle \).
questions.answer: \( \nabla\cdot\mathbf F=2 y z + y e^{x} \); at \( \left( 2, \  -2, \  0\right) \) this is \( - 2 e^{2} \).

questions.q: Find \( \nabla\cdot\mathbf F \) at \( \left( 2, \  1, \  -2\right) \) for \( \mathbf F=\langle x z, y z, x y \rangle \).
questions.answer: \( \nabla\cdot\mathbf F=2 z \); at \( \left( 2, \  1, \  -2\right) \) this is \( -4 \).

questions.q: Find \( \nabla\times\mathbf F \) at \( \left( 2, \  0, \  1\right) \) for \( \mathbf F=\langle y, - x, z^{2} \rangle \).
questions.answer: \( \nabla\times\mathbf F=\langle 0, 0, -2 \rangle \); at \( \left( 2, \  0, \  1\right) \) this is \( \langle 0, 0, -2 \rangle \).

questions.q: Find \( \nabla\cdot\mathbf F \) at \( \left( -2, \  1, \  -2\right) \) for \( \mathbf F=\langle x^{2}, y^{2}, z^{2} \rangle \).
questions.answer: \( \nabla\cdot\mathbf F=2 x + 2 y + 2 z \); at \( \left( -2, \  1, \  -2\right) \) this is \( -6 \).

questions.q: Find \( \nabla\times\mathbf F \) at \( \left( -2, \  -2, \  2\right) \) for \( \mathbf F=\langle y e^{x}, x z, y z^{2} \rangle \).
questions.answer: \( \nabla\times\mathbf F=\langle - x + z^{2}, 0, z - e^{x} \rangle \); at \( \left( -2, \  -2, \  2\right) \) this is \( \langle 6, 0, 2 - e^{-2} \rangle \).

questions.q: Find \( \nabla\cdot\mathbf F \) at \( \left( 0, \  -2, \  0\right) \) for \( \mathbf F=\langle y, - x, z^{2} \rangle \).
questions.answer: \( \nabla\cdot\mathbf F=2 z \); at \( \left( 0, \  -2, \  0\right) \) this is \( 0 \).

questions.q: Consider the surface \( S \) which is the portion of the plane \( z = 2x + 3y + 1 \) lying above the rectangular region \( R = [0, 1] \times [0, 2] \) in the \( xy \)-plane. Calculate the surface area of \( S \).
questions.answer: The surface area of a surface \( z = g(x,y) \) above a region \( R \) is given by the integral \( \iint_R \sqrt{1 + (g_x)^2 + (g_y)^2} \, dA \). Here, \( g(x,y) = 2x + 3y + 1 \). The partial derivatives are \( g_x = 2 \) and \( g_y = 3 \). Therefore, \( \sqrt{1 + (g_x)^2 + (g_y)^2} = \sqrt{1 + 2^2 + 3^2} = \sqrt{1 + 4 + 9} = \sqrt{14} \). The integral becomes \( \iint_R \sqrt{14} \, dA \), where \( R = [0, 1] \times [0, 2] \). This evaluates to \( \sqrt{14} \times \text{Area}(R) \). The area of the rectangle \( R \) is \( (1-0) \times (2-0) = 2 \). So, the surface area is \( 2 \sqrt{14} \).

questions.q: Consider the vector field \( \mathbf{F}(x, y, z) = \langle x, y, z \rangle \). Let \( S \) be the closed surface of the unit cube defined by \( 0 \le x \le 1, 0 \le y \le 1, 0 \le z \le 1 \), oriented outwards. According to the Divergence Theorem, the flux of \( \mathbf{F} \) through \( S \) is equal to the triple integral of the divergence of \( \mathbf{F} \) over the volume \( V \) enclosed by \( S \). Calculate this flux by evaluating \( \iiint_V \nabla \cdot \mathbf{F} \, dV \).
questions.answer: The vector field is \( \mathbf{F}(x, y, z) = \langle x, y, z \rangle \). The divergence of \( \mathbf{F} \) is \( \nabla \cdot \mathbf{F} = \frac{\partial}{\partial x}(x) + \frac{\partial}{\partial y}(y) + \frac{\partial}{\partial z}(z) = 1 + 1 + 1 = 3 \). The volume \( V \) enclosed by the unit cube is given by \( 0 \le x \le 1, 0 \le y \le 1, 0 \le z \le 1 \). The volume of this cube is \( 1 \times 1 \times 1 = 1 \). Therefore, the flux is given by the triple integral: \( \iiint_V \nabla \cdot \mathbf{F} \, dV = \iiint_V 3 \, dV \). Since the integrand is a constant, this is equal to \( 3 \times \text{Volume}(V) = 3 \times 1 = 3 \).

questions.q: Find \( \nabla\times\mathbf F \) at \( \left( 0, \  -2, \  -1\right) \) for \( \mathbf F=\langle x^{2} y, - x y^{2}, z \rangle \).
questions.answer: \( \nabla\times\mathbf F=\langle 0, 0, - x^{2} - y^{2} \rangle \); at \( \left( 0, \  -2, \  -1\right) \) this is \( \langle 0, 0, -4 \rangle \).

questions.q: Find \( \nabla\times\mathbf F \) at \( \left( 0, \  -2, \  2\right) \) for \( \mathbf F=\langle x y, y z, x z \rangle \).
questions.answer: \( \nabla\times\mathbf F=\langle - y, - z, - x \rangle \); at \( \left( 0, \  -2, \  2\right) \) this is \( \langle 2, -2, 0 \rangle \).

questions.q: Calculate \( \nabla\cdot\mathbf F \) at \( \left( 2, \  2, \  -2\right) \) for \( \mathbf F=\langle x z, y z, x y \rangle \).
questions.answer: \( \nabla\cdot\mathbf F=2 z \); at \( \left( 2, \  2, \  -2\right) \) this is \( -4 \).

questions.q: Compute \( \nabla\cdot\mathbf F \) at \( \left( 1, \  1, \  -2\right) \) for \( \mathbf F=\langle x z, y z, x y \rangle \).
questions.answer: \( \nabla\cdot\mathbf F=2 z \); at \( \left( 1, \  1, \  -2\right) \) this is \( -4 \).

questions.q: Find \( \nabla\cdot\mathbf F \) at \( \left( -2, \  0, \  0\right) \) for \( \mathbf F=\langle y z, x z, x y \rangle \).
questions.answer: \( \nabla\cdot\mathbf F=0 \); at \( \left( -2, \  0, \  0\right) \) this is \( 0 \).

questions.q: Calculate \( \nabla\cdot\mathbf F \) at \( \left( 0, \  -2, \  -1\right) \) for \( \mathbf F=\langle y e^{x}, x z, y z^{2} \rangle \).
questions.answer: \( \nabla\cdot\mathbf F=2 y z + y e^{x} \); at \( \left( 0, \  -2, \  -1\right) \) this is \( 2 \).

questions.q: Use the Divergence Theorem to find the outward flux of \( \mathbf F=\langle x^{3}, y^{3}, z^{3} \rangle \) across the sphere \( x^{2} + y^{2} + z^{2} = 9 \).
questions.answer: \( \nabla\cdot\mathbf F=3 x^{2} + 3 y^{2} + 3 z^{2} \). The flux equals \( \iiint_E\nabla\cdot\mathbf F\,dV=\frac{2916 \pi}{5} \).

questions.q: Use Stokes' theorem to find the circulation \( \oint_C\mathbf F\cdot d\mathbf r \) of \( \mathbf F=\langle - y, x, 0 \rangle \) around the boundary of the square \( [0,2]\times[0,2] \) in the plane \( z=0 \), oriented counterclockwise seen from above.
questions.answer: \( \nabla\times\mathbf F=\langle 0, 0, 2 \rangle \). Taking the flat surface inside \( C \) with \( \mathbf n=\mathbf k \), \( \iint_S(\nabla\times\mathbf F)\cdot\mathbf k\,dS=8 \).

questions.q: Use the Divergence Theorem to find the outward flux of \( \mathbf F=\langle 2 x, - y, 3 z \rangle \) across the sphere \( x^{2} + y^{2} + z^{2} = 1 \).
questions.answer: \( \nabla\cdot\mathbf F=4 \). The flux equals \( \iiint_E\nabla\cdot\mathbf F\,dV=\frac{16 \pi}{3} \).

questions.q: Use Stokes' theorem to find the circulation \( \oint_C\mathbf F\cdot d\mathbf r \) of \( \mathbf F=\langle - y, x, z \rangle \) around the boundary of the square \( [0,1]\times[0,1] \) in the plane \( z=0 \), oriented counterclockwise seen from above.
questions.answer: \( \nabla\times\mathbf F=\langle 0, 0, 2 \rangle \). Taking the flat surface inside \( C \) with \( \mathbf n=\mathbf k \), \( \iint_S(\nabla\times\mathbf F)\cdot\mathbf k\,dS=2 \).

questions.q: Use the Divergence Theorem to find the outward flux of \( \mathbf F=\langle x + y, y + z, x + z \rangle \) across the sphere \( x^{2} + y^{2} + z^{2} = 9 \).
questions.answer: \( \nabla\cdot\mathbf F=3 \). The flux equals \( \iiint_E\nabla\cdot\mathbf F\,dV=108 \pi \).

questions.q: Use Stokes' theorem to find the circulation \( \oint_C\mathbf F\cdot d\mathbf r \) of \( \mathbf F=\langle - 2 y, 2 x, y \rangle \) around the circle \( x^{2} + y^{2} = 1 \) in the plane \( z=0 \), oriented counterclockwise seen from above.
questions.answer: \( \nabla\times\mathbf F=\langle 1, 0, 4 \rangle \). Taking the flat surface inside \( C \) with \( \mathbf n=\mathbf k \), \( \iint_S(\nabla\times\mathbf F)\cdot\mathbf k\,dS=4 \pi \).

questions.q: Use the Divergence Theorem to find the outward flux of \( \mathbf F=\langle x, y, z \rangle \) across the sphere \( x^{2} + y^{2} + z^{2} = 4 \).
questions.answer: \( \nabla\cdot\mathbf F=3 \). The flux equals \( \iiint_E\nabla\cdot\mathbf F\,dV=32 \pi \).

questions.q: Use the Divergence Theorem to find the outward flux of \( \mathbf F=\langle x, y, z \rangle \) across the closed cylinder \( x^2+y^2\le 1,\ 0\le z\le 1 \).
questions.answer: \( \nabla\cdot\mathbf F=3 \). The flux equals \( \iiint_E\nabla\cdot\mathbf F\,dV=3 \pi \).

questions.q: Use Stokes' theorem to find the circulation \( \oint_C\mathbf F\cdot d\mathbf r \) of \( \mathbf F=\langle - 3 y, x, z \rangle \) around the circle \( x^{2} + y^{2} = 1 \) in the plane \( z=0 \), oriented counterclockwise seen from above.
questions.answer: \( \nabla\times\mathbf F=\langle 0, 0, 4 \rangle \). Taking the flat surface inside \( C \) with \( \mathbf n=\mathbf k \), \( \iint_S(\nabla\times\mathbf F)\cdot\mathbf k\,dS=4 \pi \).
